title: Group Leader – Genome Editing and Cellular Immunotherapy - Vilnius (LT) job with Vilnius University Life Sciences Center | 12866568
gist: This is a job advertisement, not an analytical article: Vilnius University Life Sciences Center seeks a group leader in genome editing and cellular immunotherapy at its EMBL Partnership Institute. The offer is a 5-year appointment with a start-up package of up to EUR 1 million and salary of EUR 60,000 to 77,000, with applications closing 27 January 2027.

insights.claim: Vilnius University's Life Sciences Center is recruiting an early-career group leader (up to 8 years after PhD) to build a program at the interface of genome editing and cellular immunotherapy, favoring next-generation CAR-T/CAR-NK, in vivo editing and engineered immune cell platforms.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Hiring priorities signal where academic genome-editing translational interest is concentrated.
insights.locator: Life Sciences Center EMBL Partnership Institute

insights.claim: The package is a 5-year appointment extendable by up to 4 years after an interim evaluation, with a start-up package of up to EUR 1 million including a salary of EUR 60,000 to 77,000 per year.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Benchmarks the cost of establishing a PI-led gene-therapy research group in Central and Eastern Europe.

insights.claim: The EMBL Partnership Institute for Genome Editing Technologies was founded in 2020 at Vilnius, and its principal investigators have attracted multiple ERC and EMBO Installation Grants.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Indicates a growing, grant-backed European genome-editing hub outside the main Western centers.

insights.claim: The newly established Translational Center for Gene Technologies (TRACEGET) provides core facilities targeting cancer, age-related diseases and gene-based therapies.
